description:
## Périmètre
- CI lecture seule : 4 serveurs DNS faisant autorité, IPv4 S1, contrôle AAAA, HTTPS/TLS par SNI, redirection HTTP→HTTPS, résolution publique informative
- Runbook S1 : responsabilités distinctes des deux sous-domaines, état des vhosts, certificats, admission des PR #1/#2, sauvegarde et rollback, interdiction d'exposer les fonctions de patch sans authentification et revue

## Sécurité
- Aucun secret ni SSH, pas de commande serveur arbitraire
- Ne change aucun vhost, aucune zone DNS et aucun déploiement
- `main` inchangée ; branche basée sur V0.2 PR #2 (stacked PR)
- Cette PR reste draft tant que la CI, les revues indépendantes et les prérequis applicatifs ne sont pas validés

## Dépendances
- PR #1 → PR #2 → présente PR
- Le MCP ne dispose pas encore d'une capacité de déploiement PHP2SHELL autorisée ; nécessité d'un mandat MCP séparé et gouverné, sans créer de gateway parallèle
- Les interfaces/API de production restent à développer ; le pipeline certifie uniquement la préparation réseau.

@@ -0,0 +1,90 @@
+name: S1 PHP2SHELL + PHPPATCH readiness (read-only)
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches:
+      - ops/s1-readiness-php-services-20261027
+  pull_request:
+    paths:
+      - ".github/workflows/s1-readiness.yml"
+      - "deploy/**"
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  s1-readiness:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 8
+    steps:
+      - name: Verify authoritative DNS, public origin, TLS and HTTPS redirect
+        shell: bash
+        env:
+          S1_IPV4: "212.227.212.33"
+          ZONE: wealthtechinnovations.com
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          declare -a HOSTS=(
+            php2shell.wealthtechinnovations.com
+            phppatch.wealthtechinnovations.com
+          )
+          mapfile -t NAMESERVERS < <(dig +time=3 +tries=1 +short NS "$ZONE" | sort)
+          if (( ${#NAMESERVERS[@]} < 2 )); then
+            echo "::error::Insufficient authoritative name servers"; exit 1
+          fi
+          {
+            echo "## S1 PHP services network readiness"
+            echo ""
+            echo "UTC: $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
+            echo ""
+            echo "| Hostname | Authoritative A | AAAA | Public route | HTTPS S1 | Redirect |"
+            echo "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"
+          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
+
+          for HOST in "${HOSTS[@]}"; do
+            echo "::group::Preflight: $HOST"
+            for NS in "${NAMESERVERS[@]}"; do
+              ANSWER=$(dig +time=4 +tries=1 +short "@$NS" "$HOST" A)
+              echo "Authoritative @$NS $HOST A: $ANSWER"
+              if [[ "$ANSWER" != "$S1_IPV4" ]]; then
+                echo "::error::$HOST authoritative A differs from S1 at $NS"
+                exit 1
+              fi
+              AAAA=$(dig +time=4 +tries=1 +short "@$NS" "$HOST" AAAA)
+              if [[ -n "$AAAA" ]]; then
+                echo "::error::$HOST has IPv6 records not covered by this S1 IPv4-only readiness gate: $AAAA"
+                exit 1
+              fi
+            done
+
+            # Authoritative data is the gate; a recursive resolver can cache an older answer.
+            PUBLIC_IP=$(curl -fsS -I -o /dev/null --connect-timeout 7 --max-time 20 -w '%{remote_ip}' "https://$HOST/")
+            echo "Public destination: $PUBLIC_IP"
+            if [[ "$PUBLIC_IP" != "$S1_IPV4" ]]; then
+              echo "::notice::$HOST public recursive resolver still routes via $PUBLIC_IP; may be stale"
+            fi
+
+            DIRECT_STATUS=$(curl -fsS -I -o /dev/null --connect-timeout 7 --max-time 20 --resolve "$HOST:443:$S1_IPV4" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/")
+            if [[ "$DIRECT_STATUS" != "200" ]]; then
+              echo "::error::$HOST did not return HTTPS 200 from S1: $DIRECT_STATUS"
+              exit 1
+            fi
+
+            REDIRECT_STATUS=$(curl -sS -I -o /dev/null --connect-timeout 7 --max-time 20 --resolve "$HOST:80:$S1_IPV4" -w '%{http_code}' "http://$HOST/")
+            if [[ "$REDIRECT_STATUS" != "301" && "$REDIRECT_STATUS" != "308" ]]; then
+              echo "::error::$HOST did not redirect HTTP to HTTPS: $REDIRECT_STATUS"
+              exit 1
+            fi
+
+            if ! timeout 12 openssl s_client -connect "$S1_IPV4:443" -servername "$HOST" </dev/null 2>/dev/null |
+                openssl x509 -noout -checkend 604800 >/dev/null; then
+              echo "::error::$HOST S1 TLS certificate expires in less than 7 days or could not be parsed"
+              exit 1
+            fi
+            echo "S1 direct TLS and redirect validated for $HOST"
+            echo "| $HOST | $S1_IPV4 | no AAAA | $PUBLIC_IP | $DIRECT_STATUS (TLS checked) | $REDIRECT_STATUS |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
+            echo "::endgroup::"
+          done
+
+          echo "Network and certificates pass. This does NOT prove app/auth/deployment readiness."

+# PHP2SHELL + PHPPATCH — S1 deployment admission (NOT deployed)
+
+## Authority and target
+
+- Repository: `chainsolutions-wealthtech/Php2shell` (public; source only)
+- S1 IPv4: `212.227.212.33` (verified MCP project context)
+- Plesk subscription: `wealthtechinnovations.com`
+- Console: `https://php2shell.wealthtechinnovations.com`
+- Remediation frontend: `https://phppatch.wealthtechinnovations.com`
+- Read-only observed Plesk folders:
+  - `/var/www/vhosts/wealthtechinnovations.com/php2shell.wealthtechinnovations.com`
+  - `/var/www/vhosts/wealthtechinnovations.com/phppatch.wealthtechinnovations.com`
+  - corresponding `/var/www/vhosts/system/<hostname>` directories
+- Both current sites show a Plesk placeholder, **not** a deployed application.
+- Two hostnames, one future shared engine, separate authorization boundaries. Never create an independent second gateway.
+
+## Live network evidence (2026-10-27)
+
+DNS A on four authoritative IONOS nameservers => `212.227.212.33` for both.
+The old IONOS parking AAAA records have been removed; MX still return `mx00.ionos.fr` and `mx01.ionos.fr`.
+HTTPS direct with SNI on S1: `200` for both, trusted Let's Encrypt certificates. HTTP redirects to HTTPS with `301`.
+PHP2SHELL certificate: 2026-10-27 through 2027-01-25.
+PHPPATCH certificate: 2026-10-27 through 2027-01-25.
+A stale recursive cache was observed (old parking IPv4 at Google DNS shortly after change).
+An *internal S1* curl by hostname still failed after the public DNS fix: `curl (6)` for PHP2SHELL and `curl (35)` for PHPPATCH. Root cause **not yet confirmed**.
+Evidence workflow: `.github/workflows/s1-readiness.yml`. It checks current DNS/HTTPS/TLS without credentials or writes.
+
+## Release gates — block until every relevant prerequisite passes
+
+1. Merge PR #1 (V0.1) only after review, verified CI and confirmed target HEAD.
+2. Finish and independently review PR #2 (V0.2). Lexical indicators are **not** confirmed vulnerabilities and the demo CVE catalogue is unverified.
+3. Implement actual API and web consoles with identity, RBAC, authentication, sessions, CSRF controls, audit log, rate limiting and secret separation.
+4. Implement and review a governed, **scoped** GitHub-to-MCP-to-S1 deployment capability. MCP currently has no generic authorized Plesk provisioning, DNS management, or arbitrary SSH command action. Do not repurpose a `legacy_vhost` command for an unrelated target.
+5. Restore reliable local DNS diagnostics on S1 via a separate governed MCP PR, with read-only `getent/dig/resolv.conf` and specifically authorized cache invalidation if shown necessary. Never flush global caches indiscriminately.
+6. Obtain a deployment authorization identifying release commit SHA, exact target path(s), runtime user and the two subdomain mappings. Do not store credentials in this public repo.
+7. Validate network preflight; CI tests, independent security review, artifact attestation, backups/rollback and documented health checks.
+8. Only then deploy a locked image as non-root with minimal privileges, and run an end-to-end staging and production smoke test, including both auth boundaries, negative authorization tests and rollback.
+9. Confirm PHP2SHELL can **report**; PHPPATCH may only prepare *proposed* patches until explicit approval. No automatic execution/patch on live systems.
+
+## Separate services
+
+| Host | Intended role | Deployment state |
+|---|---|---|
+| php2shell.wealthtechinnovations.com | Authenticated console, PHP asset inventory, permitted local project scan, evidence | NOT DEPLOYED |
+| phppatch.wealthtechinnovations.com | Authenticated review/approval service for suggested diffs and CI reports | NOT DEPLOYED |
+
+No production API or UI is presently implemented in the V0.1/V0.2 CLI repository.
+Do **not** publish a remediation API at either address before the release gates are satisfied.
+
+## Verification & rollback policy
+
+- No writes to `main` outside governed PRs; record exact HEAD and CI run.
+- `S1 readiness` workflow validates DNS/TLS/redirects but not production readiness.
+- GitHub repository changes do not automatically deploy to Plesk.
+- Keep existing vhosts in place. Never purge an existing site or alter other subscriptions.
+- Prior to a rollout, snapshot the exact target content/config and register a rollback reference.
+- On failed smoke test, revert to the last approved artifact through the same governed deployment route; do not modify protected host directories manually.
+
+## Addendum V0.2 — candidate CVE review and S1 checkpoint (28 October 2026)
+
+- The current source tree includes a **local, non-mutating advisory update proposal**: `python -m app.cli propose-catalog-update --candidate ./candidate.json --as-of 2026-10-28`. It compares validated offline JSON snapshots and **blocks unreviewed deletions/date rollbacks**; a changed snapshot cannot be promoted to a trusted production feed or a vulnerability finding automatically. Code, tests, and review evidence are maintained in PR #2, with this downstream PR #3 preserving its S1-specific controls.
+- The previous internal S1 DNS/HTTPS curl failures in this runbook are **historical observations**, not a current outage assertion. At the later S1 check on **2026-10-27 23:42 UTC**, both hostnames resolved from S1 and returned `HTTP 200` with `PleskLin` and 464-byte placeholder pages. No cause of the former errors or explicit cache purge was established. Repeat the live check before any release.
+- DNS/HTTPS readiness **does not prove application deployment**. At the cited inspection only the MCP SSH Bridge container was running; neither PHP2SHELL nor PHPPATCH was installed on S1. All application, authentication, isolated Docker, authorized scoped MCP deployment, rollback and production approval gates remain required.
+- This paragraph is **documentation only** and does not change Plesk, Docker, DNS, SSL, vhost or deployment state. It updates the downstream PR branch after a non-forced integration of the latest reviewed V0.2 changes.

@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+# Architecture cible Docker / Plesk S1 — PHP2SHELL & PHPPATCH
+
+> **Statut : PLANIFIÉ, NON DÉPLOYÉ.** Contrat complémentaire au plan directeur `docs/ROADMAP.md` sur la PR #2, et au runbook S1. Aucun changement d'architecture de MCP ni de GRT. Les paramètres techniques définitifs restent soumis au préflight et à l'approbation du propriétaire.
+
+## 1. Topologie logique (deux vhosts, une plateforme)
+
+```text
+Internet HTTPS
+  |-- php2shell.wealthtechinnovations.com
+  |      |-- Plesk S1 / certificat Let's Encrypt
+  |      \-- reverse proxy -> interface Analyse (port local non public)
+  |
+  \-- phppatch.wealthtechinnovations.com
+         |-- Plesk S1 / certificat Let's Encrypt
+         \-- reverse proxy -> interface Remédiation (port local non public)
+
+         Interfaces distinctes + autorisations distinctes
+                       |
+                  API commune sécurisée
+                       |
+       +---------------+---------------------+
+       |               |                     |
+   PostgreSQL       événements          journal d'audit
+   privé            / tâches            append-only
+                       |
+           Workers à mandat explicitement borné
+             |                       |
+       Analyse PHP locale        Propositions de diff
+       source autorisée          / tests isolés / rollback
+             |                       |
+       CVE sourcées              revue + approbation humaine
+
+Github (source/CI/PR) → chaîne MCP gouvernée existante → S1
+```
+
+## 2. Isolation prévue
+
+- **Console Analyse** : conteneur Web frontal non-root, sans accès direct aux sources clients ni aux secrets du moteur de correctifs. API accessible uniquement par réseau interne contrôlé.
+- **Console Remédiation** : conteneur Web distinct avec authentification renforcée, RBAC et approbation avant toute opération sensible. Aucun endpoint de patch anonyme ni exécution directe de commandes.
+- **API / moteur commun** : service(s) internes non exposés publiquement ; séparation stricte des mandats analyse / proposition / validation / déploiement, quotas et journaux.
+- **Workers analyse** : tâches bornées en durée, CPU et mémoire ; aucun réseau sortant par défaut, sources locales autorisées montées en lecture seule, chemins validés hors symlinks, aucune exécution du PHP analysé au stade lexical.
+- **Workers tests de correctifs** : conteneurs éphémères isolés, ressources limitées, artefact préparé dans un environnement temporaire et vérifié ; accès réseau seulement si explicitement justifié et autorisé ; pas de montage de secrets de production.
+- **Données sensibles** : secrets gérés hors Git ; bases privées chiffrées/contrôlées, sauvegardes testées, journaux sans jetons ni code privé par défaut.
+- **Sécurité Docker** : utilisateurs non-root, `read_only` quand possible, `no-new-privileges`, `cap_drop: ALL`, limites de ressources, restrictions de volumes et d'egress, images verrouillées par digest avec analyse préalable.
+- **Plesk** : seuls les vhosts et certificats existants font face à Internet. Ports internes sur loopback S1 uniquement ou réseau Docker privé ; leurs numéros seront alloués après inventaire des collisions.
+- **Autorité de déploiement** : GitHub PR+CI+revue → pipeline MCP autorisé exact-SHA → préflight S1 → sauvegarde → déploiement réversible → contrôles HTTPS, authentification et logs. Aucun SSH arbitraire ni écriture directe de code sur `main` ou S1.
+
+## 3. Ordre de réalisation sans contournement des versions
+
+| Version | Livrable de cette architecture | État |
+|---|---|---|
+| V0.1 | CLI, tests, fondamentaux de sécurité | Développé, PR #1 ouverte |
+| V0.2 | Analyse statique locale et catalogue CVE fiable | Lexical partiel, PR #2 ouverte |
+| V0.3 | Patches proposés et vérifiés en sandbox, diffs, rollback | Non implémenté |
+| V0.4 | Pipeline MCP + deux domaines S1 + Docker isolé | Préflight réseau fait, PR #3 ; runtime non déployé |
+| V1.0 | Deux interfaces Web avec moteur partagé, gestion de projets, historique, rapports | Non implémenté |
+
+Les vérifications DNS/TLS déjà effectuées sont une **préparation anticipée de V0.4**, pas une déclaration de V0.4 opérationnelle. La séparation des deux interfaces concerne des permissions et des fonctions, jamais la création de deux gouvernances ou moteurs concurrents.
+
+## 4. Conditions non négociables avant mise en service
+
+- Tranche applicative effective, tests, CI et revue indépendante. Une page Plesk ou `HTTP 200` ne constitue **pas** un déploiement de PHP2SHELL.
+- Inventaire Plesk, chemins `realpath`, ports, certificats, éventuelles collisions et données déjà présentes attestés au HEAD.
+- Implémentation gouvernée autorisée des cibles dans le MCP actuel, sans détourner les outils `legacy_vhost` d'un autre périmètre.
+- Preuves d'identité, RBAC, CSRF, protection des sessions et journaux d'audit, tests négatifs d'autorisation, gestion de secrets.
+- Exposition réseau limitée et sauvegarde/restauration/rollback testés en staging.
+- Zéro scan intrusif de tiers ; remédiation sur une production uniquement après accord explicite et contrôles requis.
